panels.general_description: Coronal contrast-enhanced abdominal CT slice with a red arrow at the aorta near the left renal artery origin.
panels.detailed_description: Grayscale coronal CT slice with the letter A at upper left. The upper part shows heart and lower lungs; the abdomen shows a large liver on the image left, spleen/stomach region on the image right, both kidneys and the lumbar spine with pelvis at the bottom. A bright contrast-filled aorta runs in the midline; a thin bright left renal artery runs from it toward the image-right kidney. The red arrow lies below the midline aorta and points up and to the right toward the aorta at the left renal artery origin, where the aortic lumen appears narrowed or interrupted by darker, non-enhancing material beside the bright lumen. The kidney on image left shows brighter cortical enhancement, whereas the image-right kidney appears larger and uniformly gray with less visible enhancement. A bright linear branch also leaves the aorta toward the image-left kidney. No scale bar, laterality letter or measurement is printed. No patient name, ID number, date, institution text or other burned-in identifier is visible anywhere in the image.

The slice passes through the posterior fossa: both cerebellar hemispheres, the brainstem, the sphenoid/ethmoid air cells at the top center, and mastoid air cells on the image right. Small bright dots near the skull base represent vessels or calcification. The green arrow enters from the image left and points to the right toward the image-left cerebellar hemisphere near the brainstem, where a subtle slightly darker region lies next to the arrow tip. The abnormality is low in contrast and its borders are not sharp. No scale bar, laterality letter or measurement is printed. No patient name, ID number, date, institution text or other burned-in identifier is visible anywhere in the image.
